taxation, governance, and infrastructure are important determinants of FDI location in developed countries, and that taxation, infrastructure, and governance (but not corruption) are important determinants in developing countries.

taxation, governance and infrastructure are significant factors for FDI in developed countries, whereas only governance and infrastructure are important for FDI in developing countries.

how host country policies influence FDI location and whether there are differences between developed and developing countries.
the impact of public policies on FDI, and the impact of these policies on FDI may depend on the level of economic development of the host.
whether the impact of public policies on foreign direct investment differs depending on the host country’s level of development.

public policies have different impacts on FDI in developing and developed host countries.

FDI is more sensitive to the quality of the host country’s institutions and infrastructure in developing countries, while in developed countries FDI is more responsive to the host’s taxation policies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDI is attracted to countries with good governance, low levels of corruption, high quality of infrastructure, and low taxation.
the impact of host country government policies is different for developed and developing host economies.
the impact of host country public policies on FDI location is not the same in developed and developing countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are important differences in the determinants of FDI across developed and developing countries, and that the determinants of the location of FDI in developing countries are not necessarily the same as those in developed countries.
host country policies that are effective in developed countries may be less so in developing countries.
public policies in developing countries have a greater influence on FDI than those of developed countries.
